entities.name: Query LpxC/FabZ
observations: 468 aa soluble enzyme candidate with predicted mass 52.0 kDa and pI 5.69.
Strong homology to reviewed bifunctional LpxC/FabZ proteins: 44.3–49.9% identity over 98.3–98.5% query coverage.
Pfam supports an N-terminal LpxC domain (residues 10–304) and a C-terminal FabA/FabZ-like dehydratase region (approximately residues 330–458).
Likely cytoplasmic based on homolog annotations and absence of a predicted membrane-spanning architecture in the sequence analysis.

source_tools.relevance: Sequence properties, homology, domains, and localization inference

entities.name: Bifunctional LpxC/FabZ
observations: Reviewed homologs are bifunctional enzymes with EC 3.5.1.108 and EC 4.2.1.59 activities.
The LpxC activity hydrolyzes UDP-3-O-acyl-N-acetylglucosamine to UDP-3-O-acylglucosamine and acetate; this is a committed step in lipid A biosynthesis.
The FabZ activity dehydrates beta-hydroxyacyl-ACP substrates to enoyl-ACP products in fatty-acid biosynthesis.
Reviewed homologs are cytoplasmic and use Zn2+ for the LpxC deacetylase activity.

source_tools.relevance: Curated UniProt homolog annotations and mapped reactions

entities.name: Lipid A biosynthesis
observations: Bifunctional LpxC/FabZ homologs participate in lipid A precursor biosynthesis, including the LpxC step in the pathway toward lipid IVA.

source_tools.relevance: Curated pathway and GO annotations from homologs

entities.name: Fatty acid biosynthesis
observations: The FabZ-like dehydratase module contributes to fatty-acid biosynthesis by converting beta-hydroxyacyl-ACP to enoyl-ACP.

source_tools.relevance: Curated pathway and GO annotations from homologs

entities.name: Zn2+ cofactor
observations: Reviewed LpxC/FabZ homologs are annotated to use Zn2+ for the LpxC deacetylase activity; transfer to the query is homology-based rather than directly experimentally established.
